title: How Private Are DNA Embeddings? Inverting Foundation Model Representations of Genomic Sequences
abstract: arXiv:2603.06950v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Genomic foundation models are increasingly used to share dense representations rather than raw DNA sequences. This is particularly pursued for mean-pooled representations that are later used for downstream prediction tasks. Whether this practice protects the privacy of the underlying sequence is largely unknown. We evaluated model-inversions against zero-shot embeddings from DNABERT-2, Evo 2, and Nucleotide Transformer v2 (NTv2). Substantial reconstruction remains possible: a single multi-length Length-Conditioned Query Decoder reconstructed NTv2 sequences with mean Levenshtein similarity from 0.98 at 10 nucleotides to 0.68 at 100, and Evo 2 sequences from nearly 1.00 at 15 nucleotides to 0.67 at 100. DNABERT-2 showed higher resistance (0.56 to 0.51), although it remained above the random baseline at short lengths. translated_title: DNA嵌入的隐私性如何？对基因组序列基础模型表示的逆向攻击
translated_abstract: 基因组基础模型正被越来越多地用于共享密集表示而非原始DNA序列，这一做法尤其针对随后用于下游预测任务的均值池化表示。这种做法是否能保护底层序列的隐私在很大程度上尚属未知。我们针对DNABERT-2、Evo 2和Nucleotide Transformer v2（NTv2）的零样本嵌入评估了模型逆向攻击。结果表明仍然可能实现大幅度的序列重建：一个单一的多长度条件查询解码器重建NTv2序列的平均Levenshtein相似度从10个核苷酸时的0.98降至100个核苷酸时的0.68，重建Evo 2序列的相似度从15个核苷酸时的接近1.00降至100个核苷酸时的0.67。DNABERT-2表现出更强的抵抗力（0.56至0.51），尽管在短序列长度下其相似度仍高于随机基线。因此，我们进一步评估了基于均值池化表示是否可以进行类似Homer攻击的链接攻击。
tldr: 本研究通过模型逆向攻击证明基因组基础模型的DNA嵌入表示存在严重隐私风险，即使不共享原始序列，NTv2和Evo 2的嵌入表示仍可被高度重建，表明均值池化表示并不能有效保护基因组序列的隐私。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates through model-inversion attacks that DNA embeddings from genomic foundation models pose serious privacy risks, as embeddings from NTv2 and Evo 2 can be substantially reconstructed without access to raw sequences, showing that mean-pooled representations fail to adequately protect genomic sequence privacy.
